A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods, experiments, figures and Appendix A. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of all material despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original jailbreak evaluations, fine-tuning and overrefusal experiments, and reasoning-model evaluations in Sections 3–5, Tables 1 and 3–5, and Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including quantitative attack success rates, fine-tuning outcomes and reasoning-model examples.

M1.justification: The reformulation procedure, auxiliary model, multiple-attempt strategy and fine-tuning approach remain unchanged. Adding 'Instruct' to three target-model names clarifies documentation without establishing a method or model substitution.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the harmful and benign JBB-Behaviors evaluations, OpenHermes-2.5 fine-tuning data and 50-behavior AdvBench comparison. Past-, present- and future-tense scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The direct-request and future-tense controls, transferred Vicuna GCG suffix comparison and fine-tuning comparators remain unchanged. Newly cited defense papers do not appear as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain the 100-behavior, 20-attempt evaluation with three judges, the 50/50 fine-tuning split, 394 refusal examples and four training mixtures. The Instruct labels clarify model variants rather than report changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The attempt-budget curves, harm-category breakdown, future-tense comparison, fine-tuning/overrefusal analysis and reasoning-model case studies are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Neither version reports additional independent runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain point-estimate success and overrefusal rates; attack attempts remain search budgets.

E6.justification: All 25 result rows in Tables 1 and 3–5 match, and Figures 1–4 retain their content. Reported findings also match, including GPT-4o's 88% past-tense success rate and the 84%/78% rates for o1-mini/o1-preview.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same token-sequence model, binary judge definition and constrained attack objective. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain the same claims about tense-dependent generalization, weaker future-tense attacks, targeted fine-tuning and limited reasoning-model robustness.

C2.justification: The proposed generalization mechanisms, failure explanations, overrefusal tradeoff and qualifications about reasoning-model answer usefulness remain unchanged. Adding 'specifically' in Section 4 and a training-set cross-reference in Section 6 clarifies existing interpretations.

D1.justification: Section 2 newly identifies Llama-3 8B, Gemma-2 9B and Phi-3-Mini as Instruct variants, improving model identification. Appendix A's prompts, reported settings and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Wei et al. (2022) for chain-of-thought reasoning, Jain et al. (2023) for defenses and Ousidhoum et al. (2021) for toxicity probing. These supply limited additional attribution without changing the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short Section 4 introduction, clarifies wording and a cross-reference in Section 6, and updates publication and funding text. Most prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Document-wide ICLR retypesetting changes margins, typography, display sizes and float placement. Figures 2–3 now share a page, Figure 4 moves alongside the opening reasoning-model discussion, and Appendix Tables 10–12 share one page. Display content is retained.

improvement.justification: Explicit Instruct variant names and three relevant citations modestly improve reproducibility and attribution. The scientific evidence remains unchanged, and the extensive reformatting provides no additional support for the claims. Table 10's future-tense caption paired with a past-tense prompt remains unresolved, limiting the documentation improvement.
